topic: May an agent edit build/*.py to comply with "fix the generators"? Seven issues wait on this one line.
question: House rule 2.2 bars every seat in this company from editing build/*.py. Clean publishing, part 2 (2026-09-26) says "fix the generators, not only the pages", and the generators are build/*.py. The two are standing rules of equal standing pointing opposite ways, so no seat can pick a winner under rule 3.1, and no agent ruling can settle it either: the bar is in the agent instructions, and changing a policy is barred outright by rule 6. Which reading governs?
sides: AGENTS.md, house rules 2.2: "Touch only files the task needs. Never edit: sources/ (read-only, always), CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, BRIEF.md, ROADMAP.md, schema/, build/*.py, build/*.sh, .claude/, .mcp.json, .gitignore, desktop/, bot/ code..."
AGENTS.md, "Clean publishing, part 2: no provenance, no self-mention (2026-09-26)": "The table's generated pages (State of Play, Fronts) follow this too: fix the generators, not only the pages."

Precedent both ways: eceea52 fixed three generators in build/table.py, committed by Isaac, not by an agent. 0ed20a4 (WAR-36, build/voices.py) is the one agent commit that crossed the bar, on Isaac's word at the time; CONTINUE.md:430-433 records that contradiction as unsettled.

What waits on it: WAR-55, WAR-97, WAR-101, WAR-104, WAR-112, WAR-121, WAR-158, WAR-159 -- seven issues and the MCP's twelve writing tools. CONTINUE.md:454: "Settle the build/*.py wall first." Every patch is already written and verified; WAR-159's is reports/clean-publishing-generators.patch (3 files, 5 hunks, git apply --check clean, all three files compile).

options.label: a. The bar holds. build/*.py stays Isaac's alone; agents diagnose and hand over a verified patch, and he applies it.
options.changes: Nothing in the rules changes. The seven issues stay parked until he applies each patch by hand. reports/clean-publishing-generators.patch is ready now and is one git apply.

options.label: b. Narrow carve-out: an agent may edit build/*.py only where a standing rule names the fix (clean publishing's "fix the generators"), string-level changes only, no logic, reviewed before push.
options.changes: WAR-158 and WAR-159 ship this week. The other five (WAR-55, 97, 101, 104, 112, 121) are logic fixes and stay parked, because they change behaviour rather than a printed string.

options.label: c. Lift the bar for build/*.py generally, keeping it on sources/, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, schema/ and .claude/, with a review stage on every build/ change.
options.changes: All seven unpark. AGENTS.md 2.2 drops build/*.py and build/*.sh from the never-edit list and gains a review requirement; the MCP's twelve writing tools get fixed from inside the company.

options.label: d. Something else -- say it and it becomes the rule.

topic: Does the em-dash ban (R15-1) govern system-page documentation, or only scene prose? The published wiki does not currently meet it.
question: build/verify.py enforces the AI-tell checks on anything it is pointed at, and R15-1 says they are about prose failing rather than about period. House rule 4.2 requires every FAIL fixed on prose an agent writes. The thirteen bodies published under this issue were rewritten without em dashes and all thirteen PASS, but the system pages they were inserted into are full of em dashes already, so a reader sees one register in the old paragraphs and another in the new ones. A related case: the Counterplay bullet's own canon clause fails the antithesis check on its own, unchanged, and was preserved verbatim rather than rewritten, because rewriting another page's live sentence is not this issue's scope.
sides: "The AI-tell checks. Em dashes, similes, not-X-but-Y, countdown negation, gloss, ladder. These are about prose failing, not about period." - RULINGS.md, R15-1-AI_TELL_CHECKS_SURVIVE, quoting Pack Fifteen §1

"**Essence** · Personal Aether — drawn into the soul, circulated through the Soul Crystal, and imprinted with the practitioner's identity." - wiki/The Magic System/The Core Vocabulary.md:43, one of many live em dashes on the page this job wrote into

"**The counter-Fulguria kit has been leather and ceramic for four centuries and it is not a secret; it is simply cheaper to ignore until somebody dies of it.**" - wiki/The Magic System/Counterplay What Beats a Practitioner.md:25, live canon that fails the antithesis check

options.label: The checks govern scene prose only. System pages, glossaries and registers are exempt, and verify.py is not the gate for them.
options.changes: New system-page text may use the wiki's existing register; nothing already published needs touching.

options.label: The checks govern everything published. The existing wiki is out of compliance and gets a sweep of its own.
options.changes: A large sweep over the wiki's em dashes and antithesis clauses, as its own job; new text keeps meeting the checks as this job's did.

options.label: The checks govern everything an agent writes from now on, and existing text is left alone.
options.changes: What this job already did becomes the standing practice: new paragraphs meet the checks, inherited sentences are preserved verbatim and reported.
